decision_conditions: <p><span id="docs-internal-guid-83c81970-7fff-0770-d8cd-363aad2b0214"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space-collapse: preserve;">The advertisement, by reason of its design, siting and scale, would result in an incongruous and dominant addition that would contribute to unsightly proliferation of clutter signage to the surrounding area, detracting from its visual amenity and would be contrary to London Plan policies D3 (Optimising Site Capacity through the Design-led approach) D8 (Public Realm) and Hackney Local Plan policies, LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character), LP7 (Advertisements), London Legacy Development Corporation Local Plan&nbsp; BC.16 (Designing Adverts), the guidance set in the Planning Practice Guidance and the National Planning Policy Framework.&nbsp; </span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-c0234567-7fff-5949-20fa-58656b902508"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space-collapse: preserve;">The advertisement, by reason of its scale and position, would have an unacceptable impact upon public and highway safety to the detriment of vehicular and pedestrian safety. As such, the proposal would be contrary to T2 (Healthy Streets), T4 (Assessing and Mitigating Transport Impacts) of the London Plan (2021) and LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods), LP42 (Walking and Cycling), LP43 (Transport and Development) of Hackney's Local Development Plan (2020).</span></span></p>
description: Advertisement Consent (retrospective) for the installation of one freestanding, non-illuminated 48-sheet timber billboard for the display of paper sheet posters, measuring 6m x 3m, for a temporary period from 1 April 2025 to 1 April 2030.
